solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Starter of smoked fish has strong smell …

indicators.note: the starter of a word is its opening letter, here of smoked

parts.note: the tench is a freshwater fish of the carp family

explanation.surface: A plate of smoked fish served as a first course gives off a powerful pong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter' looks like the menu course, but it asks for the opening letter of 'smoked'.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a stench is a foul, overpowering odour.

clue.text: Black humour, taken poorly by Japan's fine with English

parts.note: poorly means unwell or sick
J is the international vehicle code for Japan
OK means fine or all right

explanation.surface: Someone in Japan reacts badly to dark comedy, but is fine with English.
explanation.definitionFit: A sick joke is a tasteless gag about grim subjects, an example of black comedy.

clue.text: Be upstanding to execute Queen's offender

indicators.note: upstanding in a down entry means rising, so the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: to be is to exist or live
to execute a task is to do it
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A courtroom command to stand before an offender against the Queen is executed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Be upstanding' is the usher's call to rise; here 'Be' gives LIVE and 'upstanding' turns it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: an evildoer is a wrongdoer or criminal.

clue.text: Serenity found amid diabolical mayhem

indicators.note: found amid means sitting in among the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone finds peace in the middle of hellish chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: calm is a state of peace and tranquillity.

clue.text: … it's Scotland's premier fish

definitions.meaning: Nicola ... was First Minister, the head of the Scottish government, from 2014 to 2023
a large fish prized for its roe, caviar

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue's sentence, the smelly fish turns out to be Scotland's finest.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to 1 Across's fishy surface; one sense is a politician, the other the fish. Nicola Sturgeon led Scotland's government as First Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: A double definition: a surname of a Scottish political leader, and a large caviar-yielding fish.

clue.text: That week angrily heard man will get to drive

indicators.note: angrily suggests the words are stirred up, their letters rearranged
heard means we want what the spoken contraction sounds like

parts.note: a man will is he will, contracted to he'll

explanation.surface: A man, heard cursing that week, is going to be allowed to drive.
explanation.walkthrough: Anagram of THAT WEEK gives TAKETHEW; HE'LL said aloud gives HEEL.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit at the steering wheel is an idiom for becoming the driver.

clue.text: Left in check by Queen, takes his turn to resign

indicators.note: in means inside, so the letter for left sits within the word for check

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain
Qu is an abbreviation for queen, placed next to the rest

indicators.note: takes his turn means the word his is turned about, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A chess game: checked by the queen, a player takes his move and then resigns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'check' and 'Queen' suggest chess, but 'check' gives REIN; HIS turned gives ISH.
explanation.definitionFit: To relinquish is to give up or surrender something, such as a post.

clue.text: Machine has some benign effects arising

indicators.note: arising in a down entry means coming up, so the letters read bottom to top
some means only part of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: A machine with some kindly side effects coming up.
explanation.walkthrough: ENIGNE sits inside 'benign effects' and reads upwards as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine is a machine that converts energy into motion.

clue.text: Put up stone vessel for spice

indicators.note: put up in a down entry means raised, so the pieces are read bottom to top

parts.note: a gem is a precious stone
a tun is a large cask, a vessel for wine or beer

explanation.surface: Someone stores a spice in a stone jar.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutmeg is the aromatic seed of a tropical tree, ground as a spice.

clue.text: West of country's undulating and cold

indicators.note: in an across entry the west end of a word is its first letter, here of country's

parts.note: undulating land rises and falls, so it is hilly

explanation.surface: The western part of some nation is rolling countryside and chilly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West of country' looks like a region; it is just the leftmost letter of 'country'.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: chilly weather is unpleasantly cold.

clue.text: Island's briefly illuminated from high window

indicators.note: a word said briefly loses its final letter, so the island's name is cut short

parts.note: Skye is an island of the Scottish Inner Hebrides
something illuminated is lit up or light

explanation.surface: An island is lit up for a moment from some lofty vantage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' looks like 'for a moment' but trims the last letter of SKYE.
explanation.definitionFit: A roof opening glazed to admit daylight is a window set high in a building.

clue.text: Distracted sailor's shipped home having beginnings of dementia caught by doctor

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor
shipped means sent off

indicators.note: caught by means held inside, here within the doctor's letters

parts.note: MD, Doctor of Medicine, is a doctor
in means at home

indicators.note: the beginnings of a word are its opening letters, here of dementia

explanation.surface: A sailor sent home showing early signs of dementia is seen by a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginnings' is plural, so it takes the first two letters of dementia, not just one; 'caught by' puts them, after 'home', inside the doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: someone distracted is forgetful, their thoughts elsewhere.

clue.text: Judge duo performing martial art

indicators.note: performing suggests the word duo is acted out, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A pair of performers are being judged in a martial arts display.
explanation.definitionFit: Judo is a Japanese unarmed combat sport, an example of the martial arts.

clue.text: Leave money invested showing self-restraint

indicators.note: invested means put inside, here money placed within leave

parts.note: leave from work, as in leave of absence
tin is old slang for money

explanation.surface: Leaving your cash in an investment is a show of discipline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invested' reads as finance but means placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstinence is refraining from indulgence, such as alcohol, a form of self-denial.

clue.text: Cathars led building of big churches

indicators.note: the building of something puts its parts together anew, so the letters are rebuilt

explanation.surface: The medieval Cathar sect led the construction of grand churches.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cathars were a medieval Christian sect in southern France.
explanation.definitionFit: A cathedral is the principal church of a diocese, typically a large one.

clue.text: Watch for and exclude one viewer interrupting

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into, so these pieces go in the middle of the phrase for exclude

parts.note: to exclude someone is to keep them out
an means one, as in an apple
the eye is the organ that views

explanation.surface: Someone is told to watch for and bar a spectator who keeps interrupting.
explanation.definitionFit: To be watchful for something is an idiom for staying alert to spot it.

clue.text: Old man's strong — he's out making a footpath!

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, your old man

indicators.note: out means removed, so these letters are dropped

parts.note: vehement feeling is strong or forceful
taken as written

explanation.surface: Dad is strong-willed, and he storms out onto the footpath!
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage the paved walkway beside a road for pedestrians is a footpath.

clue.text: Get together before union's hard on pay and rent chaos

indicators.note: in a down entry, on means placed above what follows

parts.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

indicators.note: chaos means disorder, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A trade union pushes hard on wages, and rent arrears cause chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union' looks like a trade union but is a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebration for a bride and her female friends held before the wedding, a pre-marriage gathering.

clue.text: A new smash hit medley from somebody or other

indicators.note: a medley is a mixture, so the letters of the phrase are mixed up

explanation.surface: A medley of a brand-new hit record comes from some unnamed artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A placeholder name used for a person whose name escapes you, i.e. an unspecified someone.

clue.text: Quarrelling adds to confusion

indicators.note: confusion means disorder, so the letters of the words are mixed up

explanation.surface: An argument only adds to the muddle.
explanation.definitionFit: People in disagreement or conflict are said to be in dispute, an idiom.

clue.text: Used to be cheeky with master

parts.note: ex means former, what something used to be
pert means saucy or cheeky

explanation.surface: Someone was once impertinent to their master.
explanation.definitionFit: A master of a craft is a skilled specialist in it.

clue.text: Cabbie volunteers with club to carry team

indicators.note: to carry is to hold, so the team sits within the other pieces

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
a driver is a golf club
XI, eleven, is a cricket or football team

explanation.surface: A cabbie who volunteers for his club ferries the team around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to carry' makes the volunteers and the club together hold the team, so it lands where the two meet.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a cabbie is someone who drives a taxi for hire.

clue.text: Each filled album's bound

indicators.note: filled means stuffed, so the album has a piece inside it

parts.note: an LP is a long-playing record album

explanation.surface: Each album stuffed full is bound like a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' looks like 'tied up' but is the noun for a jump.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a bound is a big spring or jump.

clue.text: Cats purr a bit with encouragement

indicators.note: a bit means only a small part of the words is taken

explanation.surface: Cats purr a little when they are encouraged.
explanation.definitionFit: A spur is a stimulus or incentive, something that urges one on.

clue.text: Pass on meeting solid Brexiteers; ultimately they won't change their minds

parts.note: to pass on is a euphemism for to die
solid means firm or hard

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so take the final letter of Brexiteers

explanation.surface: A political jibe: Brexit supporters who will never budge.
explanation.definitionFit: Stubborn people who refuse to give up a position, however lost, are hardliners.

clue.text: Look! Man Friday's coming back with fruit

indicators.note: coming back means returning, so these letters read backwards

parts.note: a Man Friday is a loyal helper or personal assistant, PA
a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: Look, Robinson Crusoe's servant is returning with some fruit!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look!' is a verb, as in 'look happy', meaning seem.
explanation.definitionFit: To look a certain way is to seem or give an impression.

clue.text: Reserve central hotel in Margate perhaps

indicators.note: in means within, so the letter goes into the coastal word

parts.note: Margate is a resort town on the Kent coast, an example of the seaside

indicators.note: central means middle, so take the middle letter of hotel

explanation.surface: A booking at a hotel in the middle of Margate is held in reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: Margate is an English seaside resort in Kent; 'perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: To reserve something is to put it aside or keep it apart for later use.

clue.text: Briefly become oddly tatty and unpleasant

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, losing the last letter

parts.note: to grow, as in grow old, is to become

indicators.note: oddly means the odd-numbered letters of tatty

explanation.surface: Something swiftly turns strangely shabby and nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' looks like 'strangely' but picks letters 1, 3 and 5 of tatty.
explanation.definitionFit: Grotty is British slang for dingy, nasty or unpleasant.
